checks.note: Ordered-map semantics, automatic and explicit keys, append behavior, nested access, presence checks, mutations, merge, sorting, map, filter, reduce and counting agree with the official PHP documentation and exact runtime output.
The rewrite stays within the approved PHP-arrays scope and current official PHP documentation. The immutable SOURCE, candidate, draft and earlier reviews were not changed.
Every one of the 23 article examples was executed independently on PHP 8.4.26 and 8.5.11. All 46 executions matched the displayed stdout exactly, exited with code 0 and produced empty stderr.
Changed explanations and added functions are covered by current official documentation; version-sensitive null and negative-key statements remain bounded to the approved 8.4–8.5 range.

The basic path is now execution and output → key/value model → list and named keys → visible read/update/append → value types → nesting → foreach → presence → simple then advanced mutations. Edge-case key conversion and higher-order operations follow later.

Multi-operation examples label their output, overloaded mutation examples are split, unfamiliar helper syntax is introduced locally, and eleven examples explicitly expose an initial and resulting state.
Repeated state displays serve progression or contrast. No obsolete part-I/part-II framing, duplicate summary or internal workflow note was introduced.
The form-shaped example still checks type before validation and explicitly excludes a complete HTTP handler. extract() remains a warning demonstrated only with local trusted data.
The article declares PHP 8.4–8.5. Runtime claims are limited to exact PHP 8.4.26 and 8.5.11 CLI runs; PHP 8.1, 8.3 and 8.5 behavior changes are named only where documented.
No new unsupported framework, installation, web-server or application-security guarantee is made. Practical-use sentences are examples of use, not claims of complete application behavior.
